No $R$-algebra structure on $S$ or scalar-tower compatibility is assumed here. For every $R$-derivation $D:T\to T$, if $D(\iota(s))=0$ for all $s\in S$, where $\iota:S\to T$ is the structure map, then $D$ is the zero derivation.

readback.en: Write $\mathbb Q(t)$ for the intermediate field generated by $t$. For a characteristic-zero field $F$, $\partial_t$ denotes the specified $\mathbb Q$-derivation $F\to F$: if $t$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$ and $F/\mathbb Q(t)$ is algebraic, it is the formally étale extension of the derivation $p(t)\mapsto p\prime(t)$ on $\mathbb Q[t]$; otherwise it is the zero derivation. Scalar multiplication $a\partial_t$ means pointwise multiplication by $a$. A place $P$ of $F$ means a valuation subring $O_P\ne F$ containing every rational scalar, with no restriction to an affine chart. If $F$ is a curve field, meaning that it is finite dimensional over $\mathbb Q(z)$ for some transcendental $z$, then $v_P(f)=-\log(V_P(f))\in\mathbb Z$, where $V_P$ is the valuation of the maximal ideal of the discrete valuation ring $O_P$. This is a total function, with $v_P(0)=0$. The symbol $\pi_P$ is the chosen element of $F$ with $v_P(\pi_P)=1$. The canonical multiplicative valuation of an arbitrary valuation subring $O$ is denoted by $\nu_O$. namespace Place

variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [CharZero K]

structure CanonicalDivisorData (M : Model N) (hDVR : PlacesDiscrete M) where
  D : Divisor M

    D P = if M.u ∈ P.1 then ramIdx M hDVR M.u P - 1

  map_smul' q a := by simp
  map_one_eq_zero' := by simp
